minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  October 25, 2022

1. A meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by Vice
  Chair Lau at 6:30 p.m.

  Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Wendy Lau, Council Member
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Greg Palatto, BUSD
  Don Kendrick, Resident

  Chris Dransfeldt, LVPD
  Ryan, Lehotsky, LVPD
  Janessa Gonzalez, LVPD
  Frankie Cambero, LVPD
  Michelle Mata, Tri-City Mental Health
  Gamaliel Polanco, Tri-City Mental Health
  Cory Campos, Tri-City Mental Health
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Joy Lindsay, BUSD
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne
  Erin Beilstein, City of La Verne

2. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the June 28th and August 23rd meetings
  were approved.

3. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers shared that the State has released
  raw testing data and there is a nation-wide amount of
  learning loss, however BUSD students are 30 points
  higher than the California average in English and
  Math. BUSD leadership is looking at the effect of
  poverty on performance and ways to close the gaps
  by focusing on tutoring, access to programs, and
  social group liaisons. This year BUSD has a team of
  11 personnel supporting families and students gain
  access to these resources.

4. SRO Report  School Resource Officer Janessa Gonzalez reported
  that she and Tobacco Education Compliance Officer
  Ryan Lehotsky were doing presentations at schools
  and facilities including David & Margaret and local
  private schools on tobacco and drug awareness.
  Janessa also shared that the explorer program is up
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 25, 2022, page 2

  and running with seven students who are all really
  enjoying the experience.

  Tobacco Education Compliance Officer Ryan
  Lehotsky provided an update on flavored tobacco
  enforcement efforts and noted their positive impacts
  in the community. Ryan shared that there are
  increased patrols at parks around lunch and that he
  has spoken with the Saturday School students on
  vapes and tobacco.

5. Fentanyl Presentation  Detective Frankie Cambero and SRO Janessa
  Gonzalez shared their knowledge and expertise on the
  fentanyl crisis. YFAC, the Police Department and the
  school district can assist by continuing to support
  communication outreach and raise awareness for the
  dangers of this drug. Detective Cambero shared
  about the dangers of fentanyl including how prevalent
  it is as a supplementary drug. Drug dealers are cutting
  other drugs with fentanyl because it is cheaper, and
  they can appeal to a larger demographic.

  Detective Cambero and SRO Gonzalez want to create
  a program to educate students about fentanyl
  including social media posts/reels that will appeal to
  both students and parents. SRO Gonzalez shared that
  she is trying to get Narcan in every classroom and
  Mark Rodgers from BUSD shared that the district is
  currently working on this and hoping to have it
  implemented in early 2023.

6. Public Comment  Denise Fisher shared that there is an upcoming event
  on December 3rd at University of La Verne to raise
  money for the La Verne K-9 & Police Foundation.

  JR Ranells shared that the BUSD candidates were
  holding a forum at the La Verne City Hall Council
  Chambers on October 26th and it was being streamed
  via LVTV.

  Tri-City employees shared about the wellness center
  hiring event and that they are back in schools. They
  also shared about the Therapeutic Community Garden
  and that they are creating a family group

7. Next Meeting  The regular November meeting was canceled due to
  the Thanksgiving holiday that week and similarly the
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 25, 2022, page 3

  group decided to not meet the week of Christmas. In
  order to not have too much time between meetings,
  the next YFAC meeting was scheduled for December
  6, 2022.

8. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:44 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Erin Beilstein
Management Analyst
